inputs.statement: p is prime, K has characteristic p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.

n=λ+1>0 and |I|=n. The vectors (e_i)_(i∈I) form a complex basis of V. For every integer t≥0, h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v, and for t≥1, x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v. Moreover y^(λ+1)v=0 and all higher powers on v vanish. Their action matrices are x e_0=0, x e_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ; y e_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for 0≤i<λ, y e_λ=0; h e_i=(λ−2i)e_i for i∈I. For every integer r≥0 and i∈I, X(r)e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and zero otherwise; Y(r)e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and zero otherwise. Each displayed nonzero coefficient is an integer. Here binom(a,r)=a!/(r!(a−r)!) for integers 0≤r≤a; these are the usual integer binomial coefficients.

R is the subring ℤ_(p) of ℚ⊂ℂ. The map ι_M:R⊗_ℤ M→V is injective. With M_R identified with its image it is a free R-module with an R-basis of n elements and its complex span is V. Each X(r),Y(r), r≥0, preserves M and M_R. The operators x,y,h preserve M; ℤx+ℤy+ℤh is closed under the Lie bracket. For every integer 0≤r≤λ, p∤r!, so r! is a unit in R. For all i,j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit in R and Π=E_λλ, X(λ−i)Π=E_iλ, ΠY(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X(λ−i)ΠY(λ−j). Consequently all E_ij preserve M_R.

argument.text: Use the embedding from N002 throughout to regard M_R as a submodule of V. By N001 its vectors have unique coordinates in e. Since E_ii preserves M_R by N002, the ith coordinate projection maps M_R onto J_i e_i. For any i,j∈I and c∈J_j, E_ij(c e_j)=c e_i∈M_R, giving J_j⊂J_i; the reverse inclusion follows by exchanging indices. Thus all J_i equal J. Choose the R-basis m of M_R supplied by N002. The finitely many ith coordinates of m generate J_i, since each vector of M_R is a finite R-linear combination of m, and conversely these coordinates lie in J_i by E_ii-stability. Hence J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: if J were zero, every coordinate projection of M_R would vanish, so M_R would be zero, contradicting its complex span V and the nonzero basis vector e_0 in N001. Finally the maps M_R→J^I taking coordinates, and (c_i)↦Σ c_i e_i, are mutually inverse R-linear maps. The latter sum is in M_R since each c_i e_i is; independence in N001 gives uniqueness. This proves the direct sum decomposition without any rank assumption on a submodule of ℂ.

produces.statement: J_i′=J for all i′∈I; J is nonzero and finitely generated over R; M_R→J^I by e-coordinates and (c_i′)↦Σ c_i′ e_i′ are inverse R-linear maps. In particular there is a finite nonempty family of nonzero R-generators of J.

argument.text: Define U and μ as declared, and choose a nonempty finite nonzero R-generator family g_1,...,g_k of J from F001. The vectors 1⊗g_j span U over ℚ: tensor bilinearity rewrites q⊗Σ r_j g_j as Σ(qr_j)(1⊗g_j), for r_j∈R. M008 with F=ℚ, A=U and the finite set {1⊗g_j:1≤j≤k} now gives finite dimensionality of U, since this span is all of U. For injectivity of μ, write any tensor as a finite sum Σ q_l⊗c_l. Choose a common nonzero integer denominator d for the finitely many rationals q_l, writing q_l=t_l/d with integers t_l. Tensor balancing over R, which contains ℤ, rewrites the sum as (1/d)⊗(Σ t_l c_l). If its product in ℂ is zero, then Σ t_l c_l=0 because d≠0 in ℂ, so the tensor is zero. Thus μ is injective. Its image is exactly span_ℚ J, since it consists of finite rational combinations of elements of J and contains them all.

produces.statement: U=ℚ⊗_R J is finite-dimensional, μ:U→ℂ is injective, μ(q′⊗c′)=qc, and its image is span_ℚ J.

argument.text: Define T=ℚ⊗_R M_R. The inclusion R⊂ℚ gives a commutative R-algebra structure on ℚ. Apply M002 to the R-basis m: the n vectors 1⊗m_i form a ℚ-basis of T. M010 applies to the nontrivial commutative ring ℚ. M003 with this basis gives dim_ℚ T=n, since |I|=n by N001.

produces.statement: dim_ℚ T=n, and the vectors 1⊗m_i indexed by I form a ℚ-basis of T.

argument.text: Define Θ:T→U^I by Θ(q⊗Σ c_i e_i)=(q⊗c_i)_i, and define Ψ in the reverse direction by summing the maps q⊗c↦q⊗(c e_i) on coordinates. The coordinate maps in F001 are R-linear, so these balanced maps extend to ℚ-linear maps of the indicated tensor products. The composites ΘΨ and ΨΘ are identities: on an elementary tensor in a single coordinate the first is that same coordinate tensor, and on q⊗z the second is q⊗Σ c_i e_i=q⊗z. Additivity and generation by pure tensors prove the identities everywhere. Therefore Θ is a linear equivalence. Set r_J=dim_ℚ U. By F002, U is finitely generated over ℚ, and M009 says it is free. With M010 supplying the strong rank condition for ℚ, apply M004 to the finite constant family U indexed by I; it gives dim_ℚ(U^I)=Σ_(i∈I)r_J=n r_J. Apply M005 to Θ and combine with F003 to obtain n=n r_J. Since n>0 by N001, integer arithmetic yields r_J=1.

Choose a nonzero a∈J from F001. Then 1⊗a is nonzero in U, since μ(1⊗a)=a≠0. The singleton family consisting of 1⊗a is linearly independent: multiplying a putative scalar relation by μ gives that scalar times a zero in ℂ. Apply M001 over ℚ to this singleton and U, whose finite dimension is one by F002 and F004. It spans U. Consequently every 1⊗g_j is q_j(1⊗a) for some rational q_j; apply μ to get g_j=q_j a. As every g_j≠0, each q_j≠0. This proves existence of the full finite rational family needed next.

binders.type: family of nonzero rational numbers indexed by 1,...,k

argument.text: Choose q from F005, and fix 1≤j≤k. Write q_j=A/B with its nonzero integer numerator A and positive integer denominator B. By H001, p≥2, so p≠1. Apply M007 first to |A|≠0, then to B≠0, with ℓ=p. Choose d_N,u_N,d_D,u_D as in those applications, so |A|=p^d_N u_N, B=p^d_D u_D and neither u_N nor u_D is divisible by p. They are nonzero because A,B are. Hence q_j=p^(d_N−d_D)(sign(A)u_N/u_D). The rational sign(A)u_N/u_D and its inverse belong to R by the defining denominator condition, so this factor is a unit. This proves, for every j in the finite list, the claimed decomposition into an integral power of p and a unit of R, and therefore the existence of simultaneous finite families in F006.

produces.statement: There exist integers ν_j′ and units u_j′∈R for 1≤j′≤k such that q_j′=p^(ν_j′)u_j′ for all these j′.

binders.type: family of units of R indexed by 1,...,k

argument.text: Choose ν_j,u_j from F006 and let ν be the minimum of the finite nonempty integer list ν_1,...,ν_k; choose j₀ attaining it. Such a minimum exists by repeatedly taking the smaller of two integers. Put b=p^ν a. This is nonzero, since p≠0 and a≠0. For each j, g_j=p^(ν_j−ν)u_j b lies in Rb because ν_j−ν≥0. Conversely g_(j₀)=u_(j₀)b, so b=u_(j₀)^(-1)g_(j₀) belongs to J. Thus the R-module generated by the g_j is exactly Rb, and J=Rb. Under F001, every vector of M_R is a sum Σ r_i b e_i, while any relation Σ r_i b e_i=0 has all r_i b=0 by the complex independence of e in N001, and hence all r_i=0. Thus (b e_i) is an R-basis. The same spanning and independence argument works for any nonzero b with J=Rb. Together with F001, F002 and F004 this proves the exported conclusion.
